label: diffuse: input h / 1 / 2 in the original phase, plus the first copy step
explanation: Diffuse low end of a candidate neuron. Activation mass is spread out: input h (35% of mass, about 16x lift, but only 16% of h steps fire, and the h-at-t=0 activations are tiny), digits 1 and 2 (about 3x lift each), early original steps t=1..3, and the first copy step (recall_idx 1, input = first original token, 25% of mass). The largest activations (about 0.9 of max) come at recall_idx 1 when the first original token is h, j, n, 1 or k, but a predicate built on that gets precision of only about 5%. It rarely fires on late copy steps (recall_idx >= 3). Every predicate tried stays below 0.09 precision. The best compact one (h/1/2 input in the original phase, t>0) covers about 51% of mass, F1 0.14. No coherent description found.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=0: h; t=1: h, 2, 1; t=2: h, 1, 2, l) and the previous input (most: 3, l, w, x, <DEL>, v; least: i, -, g, p); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=11, t=10, recall_idx=1.
